prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and of its biologically active form, which made incretin-based therapy of type 2 diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: My configuration is unchanged: B019 alone, with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. It is the one shortlisted achievement that runs from hormone physiology (Holst on gut secretion and the incretin effect, Drucker on proglucagon-derived peptide biology and the gut and islet actions, Mojsov on the identity and synthesis of the active truncated peptide) to replicated outcome evidence in large independent randomized trials in type 2 diabetes and obesity, with cardiovascular and renal signals emerging. The mechanism is stable and decades old, so maturity is not in question. All six first-round statements converged on the same trio. I give that convergence no weight in itself, but it shows that no member found a rival reading of the discovery side. The citation is built on physiology and the active peptide forms, not on liraglutide, semaglutide or the drug class.
statement.case_against: Attribution is the real weakness, and round 1 did not remove it. Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1(7-36) form against the Habener group, who are not among the credited names, rests on recollection for all six of us, and the supplied material contains no primary publications with dates. Excluding Knudsen under the three-person cap is a cost, not a neutral choice. It will be read as favouring academic discovery over the drug development that produced the clinical impact. B002 (Walter and Mori) has the cleanest credit on the shortlist and conceptual originality that GLP-1 cannot match. If B019 credit cannot be defended, B002 is the honest fallback and not a weaker prize.

responses.point: The chair asked what the committee does if Mojsov's priority cannot be resolved from the record, whether a threshold of attribution risk would move B019 below B002, and whether B002 could wait while B019 is checked.
responses.response: I would not defer B019 so that B002 can wait. B002 loses nothing by waiting, because its credit is compact and stable. B019 is the case where the record has to be checked, and the check is the committee's job, not a reason to postpone. My threshold is this. If the primary publications show that the biological activity and synthesis of GLP-1(7-36) are due mainly to the Habener group and not to Mojsov, I would not keep her in the third place, and I would then prefer B002 with Walter and Mori over a B019 prize with a swapped name. Replacing her with Knudsen would turn the citation from discovery into development and would put Holst and Drucker beside a different achievement. If the record shows shared or contemporaneous priority, I would keep Mojsov and state the dispute openly in the committee's reasoning.

responses.point: Linnarsson said he would openly weigh Knudsen if the Habener dispute proved unresolvable, and that the trio is vulnerable if the committee judges the drug-development arm inseparable from the impact.
responses.response: I accept the second half of this argument, but I do not think it leads to Knudsen. The medicine in this achievement is the demonstration that GLP-1 physiology can be turned into therapy, and the discovery trio is what makes the citation about physiology and not about two products of one company. If the committee judges the development arm to be the decisive contribution, the right conclusion is that this is a different citation, one that probably needs a different three names. I would not smuggle that change in by substituting Knudsen for an uncertain third place. I would rather record in the reasoning that the drugs were essential to the impact and that the cap forces the exclusion than present the omission as costless.

responses.point: Perlmann asked why the credit difficulty is more tolerable for B004 than for B002, and said she would move to B002 if B019 credit cannot be settled; she also listed B008 as an alternative.
responses.response: I agree that credit difficulty is not tolerable for B004 on any three-name selection, because Boyden, Deisseroth, Hegemann, Nagel, Bamberg and Miesenböck each have a documented claim and any trio leaves a visible omission. That is why I keep B004 only as a second alternative and rank B002 first. I considered B008 but kept it outside my alternatives. CAR-T has a credit gap (Eshhar), and its credited trio is built on clinical development more than on one discovery, so it would raise the same development-versus-discovery question we already struggle with in B019. On B002 I agree with your sequencing and would go there first if B019 fails.

responses.point: El-Manira kept B019 on top but regards a UPR prize as fully defensible, and notes that early clinical translation matters less for a basic-mechanism prize; she also raised the mammalian PERK and ATF6 contributions as an open point on the Mori and Walter credit.
responses.response: I agree that the early state of UPR therapies should not count heavily against B002. The Nobel tradition does reward basic mechanism, and the yeast work of Walter and Mori defined the pathway. I also take the PERK and ATF6 point seriously, but I read it as an extension of a defined pathway and not as a competing first discovery, so it does not reopen the credit. This is why I do not treat B002 as a lesser option. Where I still differ is the ordering. A prize with documented consequence for hundreds of millions of patients and a complete discovery arc is strong enough to prefer B019 as long as the Mojsov question holds. I would revise that ordering only on documentary evidence, not on a general preference for cleaner credit.

uncertainties: Whether primary publications establish Mojsov's priority for the biological activity and synthesis of GLP-1(7-36) against the Habener group. None of us has verified this from the supplied material.
Whether the committee can state the exclusion of Knudsen openly and still defend a discovery-centred citation.
Whether B002 should overtake B019 if the attribution check turns out unfavourably.
Long-term safety and durability of incretin therapy, including weight-loss maintenance, are still being characterized.
statement.conflict_note: No change. None of the credited names on B019, B002 or B004 appears among my recorded co-authors (Kuchroo, Sonesson) or affiliations. My autoimmunity and Ro52/TRIM21 field is not the subject of any preferred or alternative item, and I do not request recusal. The chair's summary records no documented tie to any credited name for any member.
